# Ribbon Planning Tab

## How To Build

A RibbonPlanningTab should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A RibbonPlanningTab should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, integration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [Theme](../../../theme/index.md#theme): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Pitch

The ribbon's Planning tab: the commands for planning work before it is sent, as the [Planning](../../../../scope/planning/index.md#planning) says.

## Description

The Planning tab of the ribbon, between Project and Code. It takes no mode's colour: its label is in the tab row's own colour, as Project's and Application's are.
Opening it, by clicking it, with <Alt+2>, or by Ctrl+clicking it (Cmd+click on macOS) to open it alongside other tabs, as the ribbon's keyboard and opening several tabs say, opens Planning's tab in the body and selects it, or selects it if it is already open, exactly as Open Planning does, by the same route. Ctrl+clicking it while it is already open closes only the ribbon tab, and opens nothing. Switching the ribbon from Planning to another tab, or closing Planning among several, leaves the body as it is: Planning's tab stays in the body's tab bar, and the body's selected tab stays selected.

## Groups

A "Plan" group holds the Open Planning command, then New Story, then Send Sprint. An "Agent" group follows it, holding Draft Stories, then Research.

## Commands

```
openPlanning: A "Planning" button with a checklist icon. Clicking it opens the Planning tab in the body, or selects it where it is open. Its tooltip says it opens the project's stories and sprint.
  It is primary, and a full button.
newStory: A "New Story" button with a plus icon. Clicking it opens Planning and adds a story to Next sprint, its title focused.
  It is primary, and a slim button.
sendSprint: A "Send Sprint" button with a send icon, enabled while Next sprint holds a story not yet sent. Clicking it sends the sprint, as Planning's Send sprint does; its tooltip says how many stories it sends.
  It is a slim button, and not primary.
draftStories: A "Draft Stories" button with a sparkle icon. Clicking it opens Planning, or selects its tab where it is open, and opens drafting in the side panel with its "Describe what you want" box focused, exactly as the Backlog heading's "Draft stories" button and Ctrl+Shift+D do, by the same route, not a copy of it. Its tooltip says it asks the agent to break a request into proposed stories, and gives Ctrl+Shift+D (Cmd+Shift+D on macOS). It is never disabled while planning is paused, since drafting only changes the plan.
  It is a slim button, and not primary.
research: A "Research" button with a magnifying-glass icon. Clicking it opens Planning, or selects its tab where it is open, and opens research in the side panel with its "What should be looked into?" box focused, exactly as the Backlog heading's "Research" button and Ctrl+Shift+R do, by the same route, not a copy of it. Its tooltip says it asks the agent to look into a topic, read only, and gives Ctrl+Shift+R (Cmd+Shift+R on macOS). It is never disabled while planning is paused; a second research while paused keeps the pause, as Planning says.
  It is a slim button, and not primary.
```
# Body

## How To Build

A Body should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A Body should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, integration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [Theme](../../ui/theme/index.md#theme): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Pitch

The main window's body: the area to the right of the project sidebar, where the tasks sent to the harness, and the files opened in tabs beside them, are shown, and the chat input they are sent from.

## Description

Beneath the [Ribbon](../../ui/components/ribbon/index.md#ribbon), to the right of the [LeftSidebar](../../ui/components/left-sidebar/index.md#left-sidebar), which runs the full height beside it, and reaching the window's right edge. It is part of the [PromptEditor](../prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor).
The [ChatInput](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input) lives within the body, along its bottom: its left edge against the project sidebar, and above it, beneath the body's tab bar, the selected tab's contents: the message list, or an open file. While a task runs, the [RightSidebar](../../ui/components/right-sidebar/index.md#right-sidebar) runs the body's full height at its right, beside the tab bar, the selected tab's contents, and the chat input, and the chat input's right edge is against it: the chat input never runs beneath the right sidebar. While that sidebar isn't there, the chat input reaches the window's right edge.
The body is flat and quiet: the selected tab's contents, the message list or an open file, sit on the theme's base surface, #444444 in dark mode, running edge to edge with no border, and the chat input along the bottom is set apart from them only by its own darker tab strip, as the [ChatInput](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input) says, with no line between them.

## Sliding

Whenever something slides out or back along one of the body's edges, as the [RightSidebar](../../ui/components/right-sidebar/index.md#right-sidebar) does, everything else in the body moves smoothly with it, frame by frame, rather than jumping once the slide is over: the tab bar, the selected tab's contents, the Ask conversation while it shows, and the chat input all keep their right edge against the sliding edge throughout, so they narrow or widen together, in step with it and with each other. None of them lags behind another, is left at its old width until the slide settles, or runs beneath what is sliding. Their contents are laid out anew at each width as it changes, text wrapping and rows reflowing as they go: the tab bar's tabs, the chat input's text and buttons, the message list's table, and an open file's editor. A slide that reverses partway moves them back from wherever it had reached.

## Contents

Everything that can be in the body:

- a tab bar along its top, holding a Chat tab, a tab for each file open, and the Planning tab, right after Chat, once it has been opened, since nothing closes it
- the [Planning](../planning/index.md#planning), beneath the tab bar while its tab is selected
- the [MessageList](../prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list), the chat history, shown beneath the tab bar while the Chat tab is selected
- the hint shown in the message list's place before any task has been sent, or while no project is open, as the [PromptEditor](../prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor) and the [NoProjectState](../no-project/index.md#no-project-state) say
- an [Editor](../editor/index.md#editor) for each open file, shown beneath the tab bar while its tab is selected
- a task view for each task opened in a tab of its own, as its task tabs say, shown beneath the tab bar while its tab is selected
- the [AskConversation](../prompt-mode/ask-conversation/index.md#ask-conversation), in the Chat tab's place beneath the tab bar, while the chat input's Ask tab is selected
- the [ChatInput](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input), along the bottom beneath whichever tab is selected but Planning, which is the one tab without it, and beneath the Ask conversation too
- the [RightSidebar](../../ui/components/right-sidebar/index.md#right-sidebar), at the right of all of these, the tab bar and the chat input included, while a task runs or is queued, or it is opened by hand

An [InsetPanel](../../ui/components/inset-panel/index.md#inset-panel) floats over the whole window, the body included, but is never part of it.

## Ask Mode

While the chat input's Ask tab is selected, the Ask conversation, as the [AskConversation](../prompt-mode/ask-conversation/index.md#ask-conversation) says, takes the Chat tab's place in the body, filling all of it beneath the tab bar and above the chat input, as the message list fills it for every other mode: the body never splits, and nothing is shown beside the conversation. The Chat tab then reads "Ask" in Ask's colour. Selecting another mode's tab brings the message list back in its place, as it was left, and selecting Ask again brings the conversation back, scrolled where it was; the switch is at once, with nothing sliding. A file or task tab selected shows that file or task whatever mode is selected, and selecting Ask while one is shown selects the Chat tab, so the conversation is in view.

## Tabs

Along the top of the body runs a tab bar, in gpui-kit's default tab styling, across the width the message list takes: from the project sidebar to the right sidebar while a task runs, and to the window's right edge otherwise. Its first tab, Chat, shows the message list, and is always there: it can't be closed or moved. Once Planning has been opened, its tab, "Planning" with a checklist icon, comes right after Chat, and is pinned there as Chat is: it has no close button, nothing else closes it either, and it can't be dragged, so once there it stays in the bar. After them comes a tab for each open file and each task opened in a tab of its own, files and tasks together, in the order they were opened unless they have been dragged since, scrolling sideways once there are more than fit.
Planning's tab is opened from the ribbon: opening the ribbon's Planning tab, by clicking it, with Alt+2, or by Ctrl+clicking it to open it alongside other ribbon tabs, opens Planning's tab here and selects it, or selects it if it is already open, as the [RibbonPlanningTab](../../ui/components/ribbon/planning-tab/index.md#ribbon-planning-tab) says. Opening another ribbon tab, or closing the ribbon's Planning tab with Ctrl+click, changes nothing here: Planning's tab stays in the bar and the selected tab stays selected.
Just one tab's contents show at a time, filling the space between the tab bar and the chat input. The chat input stays along the bottom whichever tab is selected but Planning, so a prompt can be written while a file or a task shows. The body starts with Chat selected, and clicking a tab selects it.
Planning is the one tab without the chat input: while its tab is selected, the chat input isn't shown, and Planning fills the body from the tab bar to the body's bottom.
